options: Conjugated C=O ≈1690; aromatic bands ≈1450–1600 and 3030; methyl C–H below 3000 cm⁻¹

fields.answer: 2-Ethyl-1-butene has a strong =CH₂ bend near 890 cm⁻¹
options: 2-Ethyl-1-butene has a strong =CH₂ bend near 890 cm⁻¹
It must have a terminal-alkyne band at 3300
It must have a carbonyl at 1715

fields.label: Distinguishing the E and Z internal products
fields.selectionPrompt: Distinguishing the E and Z internal products
fields.answer: Compare their fingerprint spectra with references; generic substitution bands alone do not uniquely assign E versus Z
options: Compare their fingerprint spectra with references; generic substitution bands alone do not uniquely assign E versus Z
Use 970 for E and 700 for Z as universal rules for all alkenes
They must have identical IR spectra because they are enantiomers
fields.explanation: Both internal products are trisubstituted 3-methyl-2-pentene. The common cis/trans rules for RCH=CHR do not directly apply; E/Z assignment needs reference spectra or complementary evidence.

fields.label: Stronger effective C=O stretching bond
options: Both must have exactly equal force constants
fields.explanation: For comparable C=O oscillators, wavenumber is proportional to √(k/μ). With nearly the same reduced mass, the higher wavenumber indicates the larger effective stretching force constant; kester/kketone≈(1735/1715)²≈1.023.

fields.answer: Ketone can give CH₃CO⁺ (43) and C₄H₉CO⁺ (85); aldehyde can give HCO⁺ (29) and C₆H₁₁O⁺ (99)

Both give only the same m/z 43 acylium ion
The aldehyde can lose water directly because it has an O–H bond
